caption: Performance of different tuning methods on GLUE for RoBERTa-base and RoBERTa-large. Here we also include two random baselines: (i) S_0-model, where all the designs are randomly selected for RoBERTa. (ii) S_3-model, where we randomly assign strategies to different RoBERTa layers while following the other design choices we learn from T5 models.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the performance of various fine-tuning methods on the GLUE benchmark for two sizes of the RoBERTa language model. The horizontal axis represents the fine-tuning method, displaying categories labeled "Prefix," "Adaptor," "LoRA," "BitFit," "S₁-model," and "S₄-model," presented in that order. The vertical axis, labeled “GLUE Performance,” has a linear scale ranging from 85 to 91, with tick labels at increments of 1. Bars are grouped by fine-tuning method, with two bars present for each method: one representing the "base" RoBERTa model in blue, and one representing the "large" RoBERTa model in orange. For the "Prefix" method, the blue bar has an approximate height of 84, while the orange bar reaches approximately 86. The "Adaptor" method shows blue and orange bars reaching heights of about 83 and 85, respectively. The "LoRA" method has bars of approximately 85 and 87 in blue and orange respectively. The "BitFit" method depicts bars with approximate heights of 86 and 88 for blue and orange bars respectively. The "S₁-model" has blue and orange bars reaching 82 and 88, while the “S₄-model” shows blue and orange bars of approximately 87 and 90. The “S₅-model” has blue and orange bars reaching approximately 89 and 91. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations; the bars are simply presented in their respective colors to represent the two model sizes.
